text:
Imagine a stadium that belongs to everyone instead of one billionaire who sells tickets at outrageous prices. You would save money while watching your local team play with pride every single season. This vision is possible through public ownership models in cities across the nation today. Yes, you deserve better access to professional sports without paying exorbitant fees or taxes hidden behind complex corporate structures.

Public teams lower costs for fans significantly compared to privately held franchises that demand huge ticket scalping prices constantly. Private owners prioritize profit over community interests often by raising entry thresholds beyond what regular people can afford easily. You pay way too much now while watching a league driven solely by shareholder greed rather than local passion or loyalty ever before. How fair is it when only the wealthy enjoy live games during prime time slots?

Community control ensures that revenue stays within neighborhoods instead of flowing out to distant investors who care little about public welfare at all times. Taxes used for infrastructure would build parks and schools first if stadium deals did not steal resources from essential government programs right now always.
